GetAlerts shows shippingservice as the only entity with RESOURCE_SATURATION: 'cpu core Normal=0.00 cores -> Current=0.15 cores (+3744.6%)' and 'cpu_cfs Val: 0.594s (Throttled)', alongside 'shippingservice-p95latency: Normal=4.27ms -> Current=18.99ms (+345.1%)'. Its own 200m CPU limit is what the container is hitting (0.15 cores = 75% of limit) and being CFS-throttled, which explains the latency. checkoutservice's p95 24.23ms -> 62.82ms (+159.3%) is downstream propagation: GetServiceDependencies shows checkoutservice calls shippingservice (a leaf service called by frontend and checkoutservice), and checkoutservice shows no resource saturation of its own with normal order-flow logs. Node worker-02 CPU rose only 3.06% -> 5.09%, so the CPU burn is localized to the shippingservice pod, not the node. All three shippingservice source files (main.go, quote.go, tracker.go) are stock upstream code with no busy loop or artificial delay, indicating excessive pod-level CPU load rather than a code defect.
